 186→class RulingAction(str, Enum):
 187→    """The ruling enum from the challenge statement. Values are the wire values."""
 188→
 189→    REFUND = "refund"
 190→    COMPENSATION = "compensation"
 191→    NO_ACTION = "no action"

 193→    @classmethod
 194→    def parse(cls, value: Any, *, field_name: str = "action") -> "RulingAction":
 195→        """Parse a model's value into the enum, tolerating underscore/hyphen/case drift."""
 196→        if isinstance(value, RulingAction):
 197→            return value
 198→        if not isinstance(value, str):
 199→            raise ContractError(
 200→                "%s must be one of %s, got %r" % (field_name, _enum_values(), value)
 201→            )
 202→        normalised = re.sub(r"[\s_-]+", " ", value.strip().lower())
 203→        for member in cls:
 204→            if member.value == normalised:
 205→                return member
 206→        raise ContractError(
 207→            "%s must be one of %s, got %r" % (field_name, _enum_values(), value)
 208→        )

 212→    return " | ".join(member.value for member in RulingAction)

 218→def _require_text(payload: Dict[str, Any], key: str, agent: str) -> str:
 219→    value = payload.get(key)
 220→    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
 221→        raise ContractError("%s: '%s' is required and must be a non-empty string" % (agent, key))
 222→    return value.strip()

 225→def _require_number(
 226→    payload: Dict[str, Any],
 227→    key: str,
 228→    agent: str,
 229→    *,
 230→    minimum: Optional[float] = None,
 231→    maximum: Optional[float] = None,
 232→) -> float:
 233→    value = payload.get(key)
 234→    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
 235→        raise ContractError("%s: '%s' is required and must be a number, got %r" % (agent, key, value))
 236→    number = float(value)
 237→    # NaN and Infinity survive json.loads and slip past every comparison below: NaN is
 238→    # neither < minimum nor > maximum, so an unbounded-nonsense amount would reach the
 239→    # parties as "refund of SGD nan". Reject them before the range checks.
 240→    if not math.isfinite(number):
 241→        raise ContractError(
 242→            "%s: '%s' must be a finite number, got %r" % (agent, key, value)
 243→        )
 244→    if minimum is not None and number < minimum:
 245→        raise ContractError("%s: '%s' must be >= %s, got %s" % (agent, key, minimum, number))
 246→    if maximum is not None and number > maximum:
 247→        raise ContractError("%s: '%s' must be <= %s, got %s" % (agent, key, maximum, number))
 248→    return number
 249→
 250→
 251→def _optional_text_list(payload: Dict[str, Any], key: str, agent: str) -> List[str]:
 252→    value = payload.get(key)
 253→    if value is None:
 254→        return []
 255→    if not isinstance(value, list):
 256→        raise ContractError("%s: '%s' must be a list of strings, got %r" % (agent, key, value))
 257→    items = []
 258→    for item in value:
 259→        if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip():
 260→            items.append(item.strip())
 261→        else:
 262→            # Numbers were once coerced with str(). That invented a citation the model
 263→            # never made: '5' resolves to no rule and no pack field, so it rode into the
 264→            # ruling looking grounded while the validator, which drops non-strings, never
 265→            # saw it. A citation that cannot resolve is worse than a missing one.
 266→            raise ContractError(
 267→                "%s: '%s' must contain only strings, found %r" % (agent, key, item)
 268→            )
 269→    return items

 486→def _cited_rule_titles(ruling: "JudgeRuling", policy: Any) -> List[str]:
 487→    """The plain titles of the rules a ruling rests on, safe for a party to read.
 488→
 489→    At most 3; a title that cannot be resolved, is empty, or would leak the internal
 490→    vocabulary is skipped. Escalation rules are excluded by ID prefix before any word
 491→    check (S5): ESC-4's title "Amount above the autonomous cap" passes the word filter,
 492→    so the prefix is the only reliable gate — a ruling citing only ESC rules gets no
 493→    Basis line. Titles are the only policy content that crosses to the party — never
 494→    IDs, never the rule text, never the Judge's explanation.
 495→    """
 496→    if policy is None:
 497→        return []
 498→    titles: List[str] = []
 499→    for rule_id in ruling.cited_rule_ids:
 500→        if len(titles) >= 3:
 501→            break
 502→        if rule_id.startswith("ESC-"):
 503→            continue
 504→        try:
 505→            title = policy.rule_title(rule_id)
 506→        except KeyError:
 507→            continue
 508→        title = (title or "").strip()
 509→        if not title or not is_party_safe(title):
 510→            continue
 511→        titles.append(title)
 512→    return titles

 515→def party_message_for_ruling(ruling: "JudgeRuling", policy: Any = None) -> str:
 516→    """The message both parties receive when a ruling is issued.
 517→
 518→    Built in code from structured fields only (the operator ruling 2026-09-23, option A): the
 519→    action, the amount for a money ruling, and the plain titles of the cited policy
 520→    rules. The Judge's explanation is never relayed — it stays on
 521→    resolution.ruling.explanation for the operator console. With no policy the message
 522→    is action and amount alone.

 524→    if ruling.action == RulingAction.NO_ACTION.value:

408→def _validate_filing(body: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 409→    """Validate one intake-form submission. Raises _HTTPError on any bad field."""
 410→    category = body.get("category")
 411→    if category not in FORM_CATEGORIES:
 412→        raise _HTTPError(400, "unknown category")
 413→
 414→    filed_by = body.get("filed_by")
 415→    if not isinstance(filed_by, str) or filed_by.strip().lower() not in ("rider", "driver"):
 416→        raise _HTTPError(400, "filed_by must be 'rider' or 'driver'")
 417→    filed_by = filed_by.strip().lower()
 418→
 419→    description = body.get("description")
 420→    if not isinstance(description, str) or not description.strip():
 421→        raise _HTTPError(400, "description is required")
 422→    if len(description) > 2000:
 423→        raise _HTTPError(400, "description must be at most 2000 characters")
 424→
 425→    claim = body.get("claim_amount_sgd")
 426→    if claim is not None:
 427→        if isinstance(claim, bool) or not isinstance(claim, (int, float)):
 428→            raise _HTTPError(400, "claim_amount_sgd must be a number or null")
 429→        if not 0 <= float(claim) <= 500:
 430→            raise _HTTPError(400, "claim_amount_sgd must be between 0 and 500")
 431→
 432→    answers = body.get("answers", {})
 433→    if not isinstance(answers, dict):
 434→        raise _HTTPError(400, "answers must be an object")
 435→    questionnaire = QUESTIONNAIRES.get(category, ())
 436→    for key, value in answers.items():
 437→        if key not in questionnaire:
 438→            raise _HTTPError(400, "unknown intake answer: %s" % key)
 439→        if not isinstance(value, str):
 440→            raise _HTTPError(400, "intake answer '%s' must be a string" % key)
 441→
 442→    return {
 443→        "category": category,
 444→        "filed_by": filed_by,
 445→        "description": description,

 447→        "answers": answers,

 292→def _questions_for_party(

 295→    """The code-rendered follow-up questions to send the filing party, or [] when none.

 298→    other advocate's (S3). The word check is a backstop, not the source of the
 299→    wording. Template questions for blank intake fields are a FALLBACK, emitted
 300→    only when no rendered question survives — a rendered question is never
 301→    doubled by a template for the field it already asks about. Near-duplicates
 302→    collapse on a normalised form (lowercase, punctuation dropped, whitespace
 303→    collapsed), keeping the first original wording. The list is capped at 3; if
 304→    nothing survives, the run does not stop (an empty needs_info is worse than none).
 305→    """
 306→    if dispute.filed_by == "rider":
 307→        collected = list(rider_case.follow_up_questions) + list(driver_case.follow_up_questions)

 310→

 312→    seen: set = set()
 313→    for question in collected:

 317→        if not text or not is_party_safe(text):

 331→    labels = dict(INTAKE_QUESTIONS.get(dispute.category, ()))

 334→        for key in labels
 335→        if isinstance(dispute.intake.get(key), str) and not dispute.intake[key].strip()
